userMessage: Draft the action plan for county_id HVA91 (Åland).

claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in Åland was 2.4% above the national level (ratio 1.024, 95% interval 0.958-1.093), about 1.9 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.

sources.label: Statistics Finland: causes of death 13u5 and 11az, population 14wx

facts.measure: age-standardised cancer mortality ratio, county relative to Finland (1 = national level)

claims.text: No measured pathway stage shows Åland clearly worse than the country; if outcomes differ, the cause is not locatable from public data.

pathway_stages_measurable_from_public_da: first contact and primary care access

claims.text: Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

statistics_not_published_by_county_for_a: time from diagnosis to first treatment
facts.goal_3_indicator_that_therefore_cannot_b: patients access treatment within the established target times

claims.text: Recommended: standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral. Under the stated assumptions this postpones about 1.4 deaths a year in Åland (range 0.2-2.8) for an assumed EUR 46,254 a year; it stayed in the portfolio in 94% of sensitivity runs.

facts.recommended_action: Standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral
facts.nature_of_estimate: model scenario under stated assumptions, not a measured effect

claims.text: First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.

facts.recommended_first_step_for_every_county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
facts.reason: The Goal 3 indicator "treatment within target times" cannot be computed from open data today. Without it no county can see where its own pathway loses time.

output.label: SCENARIO: model output under stated assumptions, not a measured effect
output.settings: default (stored in app.json, with sensitivity ranges)
output.note: Screening actions are scored on participation, not mortality; they are not part of the budgeted mortality portfolio.

output.title: Standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral
output.action: Adopt national cancer-specific pathways with maximum times per step and a single fast-track referral from primary care, following the Danish and Swedish model.
output.accountable_owner: Wellbeing services county, coordinated nationally by FICAN
output.mechanism: One referral criterion and booked slots replace sequential queues between primary care, imaging and the specialist clinic.

indicator_to_monitor.title: Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants

output.what_remains_unknown: Danish evidence is before/after without a control group. Patients left outside the pathway waited 4 days longer, so coverage must be monitored.

evidence.finding: After Denmark introduced standardised cancer patient pathways, the median diagnostic interval was 17 days shorter in 2010 than in 2004/05; patients not referred to a pathway waited 4 days longer.
evidence.unit: days, median diagnostic interval after vs before
evidence.citation: Jensen H, Tørring ML, Olesen F, Overgaard J, Fenger-Grøn M, Vedsted P. Diagnostic intervals before and after implementation of cancer patient pathways. BMC Cancer 2015;15:308.
evidence.caveat: Before/after without control group; two-tier risk for patients outside the pathway.

evidence.finding: Danish patients referred through a cancer patient pathway had a 1-year excess hazard ratio of 0.86 (0.73-1.01) vs patients not referred; 3-year relative survival rose from 45% to 54% across the implementation period.
evidence.unit: 1-year excess hazard ratio, pathway-referred vs not
evidence.citation: Jensen H, Tørring ML, Vedsted P. Prognostic consequences of implementing cancer patient pathways in Denmark. BMC Cancer 2017;17:627.
evidence.caveat: Interval includes 1; lead-time and secular-trend bias acknowledged by authors.

evidence.finding: Currently no unified national system guides disease-specific care guidelines or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways; existing guidelines, pathways, targets and indicators are not coordinated nationally, which perpetuates regional inequalities in access to and effectiveness of cancer care.

heading.fi: Toimenpide 3.1.2 Laaditaan syöpäkohtaiset hoitoketjukuvaukset, ja niiden pohjalta sovelletut alueelliset hoitoketjut, sekä mekanismi niiden ylläpitoon ja hallintaan

primaryMeasure.title_en: Write cancer-specific care pathway descriptions, regional pathways adapted from them, and a mechanism to maintain and manage them

keyText.fi: Kansalliset hoitoketjut kuvataan hyödyntäen pohjoismaissa kehitettyjä malleja.
keyText.en: National pathways are described using models developed in the Nordic countries (the text names Denmark's Kræftpakkeforløb, Sweden's SVF and Norway's Pakkeforløp).

keyText.fi: Ketjuissa määritellään ja sovitaan mm. työnjaosta eri toimijoiden välillä, tavoitelluista hoitoonpääsyajoista, keskeisistä laatu- ja vaikuttavuusindikaattoreista sekä kirjaamis- ja koodistokäytännöistä.
keyText.en: The pathways define and agree, among other things, the division of work, target access times, the key quality and effectiveness indicators, and recording and coding practices.

owner.fi: Vastuutaho: FICAN (kansallinen koordinaatio, prosessin hallinta ja tukitoiminnot sekä alueellinen käyttöönotto ja seuranta) yhteistyössä kansallisten monialaisten syöpäryhmien kanssa (hoitoketjujen sisällöt), hyvinvointialueet ja HUS (hoitoketjujen toteutus).

primaryMeasure.owner_en: FICAN with the national multidisciplinary cancer groups (pathway content); wellbeing services counties and HUS (implementation)

resource.fi: Resurssi: Toteutetaan osana toimenpiteessä 3.1.1 kuvattua kokonaisresursointia.

schedule.fi: 2026–2028: Kansalliset hoitoketjukuvaukset tehty viidestä syövästä ja syöpäkohtaiset hoitoonpääsyajat on määritetty.
schedule.en: 2026–2028: national pathway descriptions done for five cancers and cancer-specific access times defined.

schedule.fi: 2029–2031: Kansalliset hoitoketjukuvaukset laadittu kaikista merkittävistä syövistä/ syöpäryhmistä.

metrics.fi: Mittari: Potilaat pääsevät hoitoon tavoiteaikojen puitteissa.
metrics.en: Patients access treatment within the target times.

relatedMeasures.title_en: Support a smooth transfer to specialised care by defining standardised referral criteria within national care pathways, so that patients with possible cancer symptoms who meet them are sent quickly to the diagnostic tests they need
relatedMeasures.owner_en: FICAN (coordination and roll-out) with the national multiprofessional cancer groups

relatedMeasures.title_en: Define national quality and effectiveness targets and monitoring indicators so that care pathways can be monitored
relatedMeasures.owner_en: FICAN with the national cancer diagnostics and treatment steering group (shared indicators) and the national multidisciplinary cancer groups (cancer-specific targets and indicators); THL (methodological support)

output.reading_en: 3.1.2 writes cancer-specific national pathways on the Danish, Swedish and Norwegian models with target access times; 2.5.2 adds standardised referral criteria from primary care. Together they are this action.
output.gap_en: SAMA's action text says 'maximum times per step'. The roadmap leaves the values to 3.1.2 (five cancers in 2026–2028); SAMA proposes no values of its own.

thresholdRelabels.location: src/recommend.mjs INTERVENTIONS timed-pathways.action ('maximum times per step')
thresholdRelabels.relabel_en: Maximum times per step are placeholders until roadmap measure 3.1.2 defines cancer-specific access times (five cancers, 2026–2028) and 3.1.4 sets the targets and indicators. SAMA proposes no values.

indicator_to_monitor.title: Share of new cancer cases with all four timestamps recorded

output.what_remains_unknown: No health effect is modelled: this is the measurement that makes the other actions accountable.

evidence.finding: National Cancer Strategy 2026-2035, objective 3 'Ensuring equal and effective cancer care': five-year survival of poor-prognosis cancers reaches the Nordic level (lung +14 pp, pancreas +6 pp, liver +14 pp vs the 2023 NORDCAN level; Nordic = mean of Sweden and Norway); cancer mortality decreases by 10% (currently 13,300 deaths per year); patients access treatment within the established target times (THL Ohjaus 21/2016).
evidence.citation: Ministry of Social Affairs and Health / FICAN. National Cancer Strategy 2026-2035. Figure 1 and section 3.

evidence.finding: Currently no unified national system guides disease-specific care guidelines or the implementation and monitoring of care pathways; existing guidelines, pathways, targets and indicators are not coordinated nationally, which perpetuates regional inequalities in access to and effectiveness of cancer care.

output.statement: Serves roadmap measure 3.2.1; the roadmap does not name this specific action.

heading.fi: Toimenpide 3.2.1 Luodaan lainsäädännöllinen pohja THL:n Syöpärekisterin yhteyteen perustettavalle syövän hoidon laaturekisterille

primaryMeasure.title_en: Create the legal basis for a cancer care quality register at THL's Cancer Registry

keyText.fi: Perustetaan THL:n Syöpärekisterin yhteyteen kansallinen syövän hoidon laaturekisteri.
keyText.en: A national cancer care quality register is set up at THL's Cancer Registry.

owner.fi: Vastuutaho: STM (asetusmuutos), THL/Suomen Syöpärekisteri (syövän laaturekisterin perustaminen ja ylläpito), FICAN.

primaryMeasure.owner_en: STM (decree change), THL / Finnish Cancer Registry (establishes and maintains the register), FICAN

schedule.fi: 2029–2031: Syövän laaturekisteri tuottaa vähintään viiden eri syövän vuosittaiset raportit

metrics.fi: Mittari: Laaturekisterin tietopohja (ml. levinneisyystieto) mahdollistaa laadun ja vaikuttavuuden luotettavan arvioinnin ja vertailun (tietopohjan kattavuus 90 %); Kliinisten syöpäilmoitusten määrä (tavoitteena 90 % tapauksista automatisoidusti vuoteen 2030 mennessä).
metrics.en: Register data (including stage) allow reliable assessment and comparison of quality and effectiveness (coverage 90%); clinical cancer notifications (target: 90% of cases automated by 2030).

relatedMeasures.title_en: Define and start peer-development processes that compare and review quality register data systematically
relatedMeasures.owner_en: FICAN (organises peer review and peer development), THL

output.reading_en: Recording first contact, referral, diagnosis and treatment dates in the national quality register is what the 3.1.2 metric 'patients access treatment within the target times' needs before it can be computed, and what 3.2.2's county benchmarking and 4.1.3's live views of treatment start delays would read.
output.gap_en: The roadmap does not list these four dates, the entry route, or quarterly county medians. Which timestamps the register holds is left to 3.1.4 and the register work in 3.2.1.
noRoadmapMeasureFor: quarterly publication of county-level medians (3.2.2 has annual peer reviews and publicly reported regional indicators, without a frequency for publication)

Replace these values when they are published.

roadmap.titleEn: Finland's National Cancer Strategy 2026–2035: Roadmap for implementation for 2026–2031
roadmap.note: Finnish quotes are verbatim from the roadmap (see manifest quoteRule). English text is the SAMA team's own reading and translation, not an official one. A mapping says which roadmap measure an action would serve; it is not an endorsement by the roadmap's authors.

output.title: The same fast lane in public primary care that occupational care already gives
output.action: Same-week physician assessment and direct-access diagnostics for red-flag symptoms in public health centres, regardless of employment or insurance.
output.mechanism: In the Finnish DLBCL cohort the public route took a mean 207 days from symptom to treatment against 123 days through private or occupational care; most of the difference arises before the specialist visit.

indicator_to_monitor.title: Waiting time for elective outpatient medical visit (physician) in primary health care exceeds 7 days from assessment of the need for treatment, % appointments kept

output.what_remains_unknown: The route gap is observational and from one cancer type. How much of it a fast lane closes is a scenario parameter, not a measured effect.

evidence.finding: Finnish DLBCL cohort (n=160): mean cumulative days from symptom onset via private/occupational vs public primary care: first contact 42 vs 72, physician visit 43 vs 94, referral 77 vs 147, specialist visit 118 vs 204, treatment start 123 vs 207.
evidence.unit: days (mean symptom-to-treatment, public primary care minus private/occupational: 207 vs 123)
evidence.citation: Kuitunen H, et al. Socioeconomic Status and Access to Treatment in Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma. Cancer Med 2026;15(5):e71920, Figure 1.
evidence.caveat: Single cancer type, n=39 vs n=48, observational. Used as a labelled transferable prior for the shape of the route gap, not as a measured value for other cancers.

evidence.finding: Median symptom-to-treatment interval was 76 days via private/occupational care and 127 days via public primary care appointments.
evidence.unit: days (median symptom-to-treatment, 127 public vs 76 private/occupational; p=0.027)
evidence.citation: Kuitunen H, et al. Cancer Med 2026;15(5):e71920.

evidence.finding: In Finnish DLBCL, a symptom-to-biopsy interval over 7 weeks was associated with lower 2-year progression-free survival (74% vs 89%).
evidence.citation: Tokola S, et al. Cancer Med 2025;14(22):e71409.
evidence.caveat: Observational; no hazard ratio in the abstract.

output.statement: Serves roadmap measure 2.5.2; the roadmap does not name this specific action.

heading.fi: Toimenpide 2.5.2 Tuetaan sujuvaa siirtymää erikoissairaanhoitoon määrittämällä kansallisiin hoitoketjuihin kuuluvat standardoidut lähetekriteerit, joiden täyttyessä mahdollisista syöpäoireista kärsivät potilaat ohjataan nopeasti tarvittaviin diagnostisiin tutkimuksiin

primaryMeasure.title_en: Support a smooth transfer to specialised care by defining standardised referral criteria within national care pathways, so that patients with possible cancer symptoms who meet them are sent quickly to the diagnostic tests they need

keyText.fi: Kuvataan oirelähtöiset toimintamallit, perusterveydenhuollon tutkimusvastuut, suorat tutkimusreitit sekä tarvittaessa nopeat hoitoon pääsyn ratkaisut.
keyText.en: Symptom-based operating models, primary care's testing responsibilities, direct test routes and, where needed, fast-access solutions are described.

owner.fi: Vastuutaho: FICAN (kehitystyön koordinaatio ja toimintamallien jalkauttaminen ja toimeenpanoalueilla) yhteistyössä kansallisten moniammatillisten syöpäryhmien kanssa.

primaryMeasure.owner_en: FICAN (coordination and roll-out) with the national multiprofessional cancer groups

resource.fi: Toteutetaan osana osatavoitteen 3.1 mukaista kansallista hoitoketju- ja hoitosuositustyötä.

resourceShared.fi: Resurssi: Arvioitu tarvittava määräraha 5 000 000 € / vuosi (yhteensä 25 000 000 € / 5 vuotta, mikä kattaa myös toimenpiteiden 2.5.2, 3.1.2, 3.1.3, 3.1.4 sekä 4.3.2 toteutuksen).
resourceShared.en: Funded from measure 3.1.1: EUR 5,000,000 a year (EUR 25,000,000 over 5 years), which also covers measures 2.5.2, 3.1.2, 3.1.3, 3.1.4 and 4.3.2.

schedule.fi: 2026–2028: Standardoidut lähetekriteerit ja oirelähtöiset toimintamallit sisällytetty vähintään viiden yleisimmän syövän kansallisiin hoitoketjukuvauksiin. Pilotointi ja käyttöönotto käynnistetty hyvinvointialueilla.
schedule.en: 2026–2028: standardised referral criteria and symptom-based models included in the national pathway descriptions of at least the five most common cancers; piloting and deployment started in wellbeing services counties.

schedule.fi: 2029–2031: Standardoidut lähetekriteerit ja toimintamallit sisällytetty kaikkiin merkittäviin syöpäkohtaisiin hoitoketjukuvauksiin.

metrics.fi: Mittari: Vähintään 70 % syövistä diagnosoidaan levinneisyysluokissa I–II vuoteen 2035 mennessä.
metrics.en: At least 70% of cancers diagnosed at stage I–II by 2035.

metrics.fi: Mittari: Ohjeistukset (lähetekriteerit ja toimintamallit) on sisällytetty osaksi kaikkia valtakunnallisia hoitoketjuja.

relatedMeasures.title_en: Improve access to care by adding physician capacity in primary care, for example by extending the named-GP model nationwide
relatedMeasures.owner_en: STM (national implementation, steering and funding of the named-GP programme); wellbeing services counties, HUS and the City of Helsinki (deploying named-GP models)

output.reading_en: 2.5.2 describes 'direct test routes' and fast-access solutions from primary care, and 2.5.1 adds primary-care physician capacity. A same-week assessment with direct-access diagnostics in public health centres is one way to deliver both.
output.gap_en: No measure targets the gap between public primary care and occupational or private care. The roadmap describes that gap only as background (pages 10-11).
noRoadmapMeasureFor: equalising access between public health centres and occupational or private care

roadmap.title: Kansallinen syöpästrategia 2026–2035 – Toimeenpanon tiekartta vuosille 2026–2031
roadmap.titleEn: Finland's National Cancer Strategy 2026–2035: Roadmap for implementation for 2026–2031
roadmap.note: Finnish quotes are verbatim from the roadmap (see manifest quoteRule). English text is the SAMA team's own reading and translation, not an official one. A mapping says which roadmap measure an action would serve; it is not an endorsement by the roadmap's authors.

actions.action: Åland adopts standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral from primary care, following the Danish and Swedish model.
actions.rationale: The brief recommends timed pathways for Åland and the portfolio scenario estimates 1.4 deaths postponed per year (range 0.2-2.8) at an assumed cost of EUR 46,254 a year, with the action staying in 94% of sensitivity runs.
actions.owner_role: Wellbeing services county, coordinated nationally by FICAN.
actions.indicator: Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants.

actions.action: Åland adds first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publishes county-level medians quarterly.
actions.rationale: The brief states that time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county, so the Goal 3 indicator cannot be checked from open data for Åland.
actions.owner_role: FICAN with THL and the Finnish Cancer Registry.
actions.indicator: Share of new cancer cases with all four timestamps recorded.

actions.action: Åland provides same-week physician assessment and direct-access diagnostics for red-flag symptoms in public health centres, regardless of employment or insurance.
actions.rationale: The brief shows no measured pathway stage where Åland is clearly worse than the country, so the equal-fast-lane action targets the unmeasured primary-care delay that the DLBCL cohort evidence associates with longer symptom-to-treatment intervals.
actions.indicator: Waiting time for elective outpatient medical visit (physician) in primary health care exceeds 7 days from assessment of the need for treatment, % appointments kept.

obj.evidence_does_not_support: The evidence does not support that any of these actions will postpone deaths in Åland: the timed-pathways estimate is a model scenario under stated assumptions, the DLBCL route gap is observational from one cancer type, and the timestamps action has no modelled health effect.

actions.title: Standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral

roadmap.title_en: Write cancer-specific care pathway descriptions, regional pathways adapted from them, and a mechanism to maintain and manage them

sentences.text: Åland adopts standardised, timed cancer pathways with a fast-track referral from primary care, following the Danish and Swedish model.

The brief recommends timed pathways for Åland and the portfolio scenario estimates 1.4 deaths postponed per year (range 0.2-2.8) at an assumed cost of EUR 46,254 a year, with the action staying in 94% of sensitivity runs.
Wellbeing services county, coordinated nationally by FICAN.
Patients waiting over 6 months during the year for access to specialised health care per 10 000 inhabitants.

actions.title: Record four pathway timestamps for every cancer patient

roadmap.title_en: Create the legal basis for a cancer care quality register at THL's Cancer Registry

sentences.text: Åland adds first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publishes county-level medians quarterly.
The brief states that time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county, so the Goal 3 indicator cannot be checked from open data for Åland.
FICAN with THL and the Finnish Cancer Registry.
Share of new cancer cases with all four timestamps recorded.

actions.title: The same fast lane in public primary care that occupational care already gives

roadmap.title_en: Support a smooth transfer to specialised care by defining standardised referral criteria within national care pathways, so that patients with possible cancer symptoms who meet them are sent quickly to the diagnostic tests they need

sentences.text: Åland provides same-week physician assessment and direct-access diagnostics for red-flag symptoms in public health centres, regardless of employment or insurance.

The brief shows no measured pathway stage where Åland is clearly worse than the country, so the equal-fast-lane action targets the unmeasured primary-care delay that the DLBCL cohort evidence associates with longer symptom-to-treatment intervals.
Wellbeing services county primary care.
Waiting time for elective outpatient medical visit (physician) in primary health care exceeds 7 days from assessment of the need for treatment, % appointments kept.

evidenceLimit.text: The evidence does not support that any of these actions will postpone deaths in Åland: the timed-pathways estimate is a model scenario under stated assumptions, the DLBCL route gap is observational from one cancer type, and the timestamps action has no modelled health effect.
